transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Um... I hope I'm in the right place. My supervisor actually kind of told me I needed to come see someone? 

I work in production, and... well, I guess I've been having a little bit of trouble just staying at my station. I really don't mean to cause any issues, I promise. But I keep, like, popping up during our shift meetings or stepping away when I'm really supposed to stay put. My boss says it's becoming a safety problem, which I feel so bad about. I don't do it on purpose, I just kind of take off before I even think about it, you know? 

Is that... is that something that's okay for me to be here for?
When you were a child, did you also have a hard time staying seated or waiting your turn?

Um, yeah... I guess I've always been a little bit like that. I really tried to be good, I promise! But even back in, like, elementary school, I was kind of the kid who just couldn't stay in her seat. 

I didn't mean to be disruptive or anything, but I'd accidentally talk over the teacher sometimes, or... well, my mom used to get notes sent home a lot because I kept blurting things out or just wandering around the room when we were supposed to be doing our work. I just had so much energy, and I'd forget the rules for a second. 

I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this... is that the kind of thing you meant?
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable compared with your normal self?

Um, no... I don't think so. I mean, I try to be a pretty positive person! I don't really get super irritable or mad at people, I promise. I just get kind of... wound up, I guess? But never like, unusually high or anything like that. 

I just feel like my normal self, just... moving too fast sometimes, if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining that right. Is it okay that I haven't felt like that?
Do you often have trouble paying attention or staying focused on tasks?

Um... I mean, I try really hard to focus, I really do! But... yeah, sometimes it's a little tough. Like when I'm doing the inventory logs at work, or... or reading those training pages for the CNC machines. 

I always start out really wanting to do a good job, and I'm paying attention, but then... after just a few minutes, it's like the numbers or the words just kind of start blurring together? And I realize I didn't take any of it in, so I have to keep going back and starting over. I feel so silly when it happens. I don't want my supervisor to think I'm not trying, because I promise I am. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you often lose things you need for work or daily life, like tools, papers, keys, or your phone?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try to be really careful with my things! I know how important it is to keep track of stuff, especially at work. I always try to put my keys in the same spot, and I keep my phone in my pocket so I don't leave it anywhere. 

I guess everyone misplaces something every once in a long while, right? But I definitely wouldn't say I lose things often. I really do my best to be responsible with my tools and papers and everything. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just try really hard to stay organized.
Do you often forget things you were supposed to do, like tasks at work, errands, or appointments?

Um... gosh. I really hate admitting this. I don't want you to think I'm a bad employee, because I really do try to do everything right. But... yeah, I guess I do forget normal stuff a lot. 

Just... little things, you know? Like, um, clocking a step on the production checklist, or... or remembering to answer a text from my supervisor. Or sometimes I'll get all the way to the floor and realize I forgot to bring my safety glasses from my locker. 

It's so embarrassing. I get so worried because it makes it look like I just don't care about my job, but I promise I do! I care a lot, and I always feel awful when I drop the ball. It's just an honest mistake when it happens. Is... is that something a lot of people struggle with? I hope I don't sound too terrible.
Do you often feel physically restless or fidget a lot, like needing to move your hands or feet?

Oh, um... I try so hard not to do this, because I know it can be really annoying to other people. But... yeah, I guess I do fidget. 

Like, if I have to sit down for a certification class or... or one of our safety meetings at the plant? I really, really want to just sit perfectly still and be respectful to whoever is talking. But my foot just starts bouncing on its own. And I'll catch myself clicking a pen over and over, or... or picking at my sleeves, just doing something with my hands. 

I end up shifting around in my seat so much that... well, sometimes the people sitting next to me actually ask me to stop. I always feel terrible when they do, and I apologize right away! I really don't mean to be disruptive, I promise. I just get this... I don't know, this feeling where I just have to move. 

Is that okay? I mean, is it normal to just have a lot of nervous energy like that? I hope it doesn't make me seem disrespectful.
Do these same kinds of problems happen outside of work too?

Um, outside of work? I... I don't really think so. I mean, when I'm at home or just hanging out with friends, I really try to just be relaxed and go with the flow. There isn't as much pressure, so there isn't as much for me to mess up, you know? 

I always try to be super helpful around the house and not be a burden to anyone. And I haven't really had anyone outside of the plant complain about me fidgeting or anything like that. I mean, I really hope my friends don't secretly think I'm annoying! But no, I haven't really noticed it being an issue when I'm not on the clock. 

That's a good sign, right? Like, it means I'm mostly doing okay? I really do want to be doing okay.
When you get up or leave your station, is it usually because you suddenly feel anxious or tense?

Um, anxious? No, I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I definitely get worried about doing a good job, like I said before, but when I get up, it's not because I'm feeling tense or having a panic attack or anything bad like that. 

I just... I just get up because I have a lot of energy, I guess? Sometimes I just feel like I need to stretch my legs or grab a quick drink of water. It's never because I'm upset. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude at work and not let things get to me. 

So, no, I wouldn't say it's anxiety. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Before you started this job, did your restlessness or impulsive behavior ever cause problems at home, at school, or with friends?

Um... well... I guess, yeah. I mean, I try really hard to be good now, but... back when I was younger, it was a little bit of a problem. I feel so bad even thinking about it, because I know teachers work so hard, you know? 

But... even in elementary school, I was kind of the kid who just couldn't stay in my seat. I really didn't mean to be disrespectful! I just... I would accidentally talk over the teacher, or... or I'd get notes sent home to my parents because I kept blurting things out or just wandering around the room during lessons. 

I was just really eager and had way too much energy, I think? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid. I really wasn't trying to be naughty or make anyone's job harder, I promise. Does... does that answer your question okay?
When you’re at home, do you still find yourself getting up, pacing, or interrupting people a lot?

Um, at home? Oh, no, I really try to be super respectful of my family. I mean, I live with my mom and my sister, and they work hard too, so I'd never want to be a bother to them. 

I guess... maybe I get up to grab a snack or do a chore, but it's not like pacing or anything weird. I just like to be helpful, you know? Keeping busy around the house is a good thing, right? And I definitely don't interrupt them! I always try to listen when they're talking about their day. I really want them to know I care. 

So, yeah, I'm pretty sure I'm doing okay at home. I mean, I hope I am. Does that sound like a normal way to be at home?
Outside of work, do your family or friends ever complain that you interrupt them?

Um... well... I guess maybe they do, sometimes? I really try not to, I promise! I just... I get so excited to be part of the conversation, or I think I know what they're going to say, and it just kind of slips out. 

It happens at work sometimes too, if I'm being completely honest. Like, I'll accidentally jump into my coworkers' conversations, or... or if the lead is explaining something, I might answer before they're even done talking. I don't mean to be rude at all! I just want to show that I understand and that I'm paying attention, you know? 

But... yeah, I think people do get a little irritated with me when I do that. I feel so terrible when I realize I've cut someone off. I'm really trying to work on being a better listener and waiting my turn. I know it's important to let people finish their thoughts. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad person or a terrible friend. I really do mean well. Is... is it normal to struggle with that sometimes?
Do you often make careless mistakes because you miss details?

Um... oh, I really hope not! I mean, I try so, so hard to do everything exactly the way my supervisor wants it. 

I work on the production line, and I know how important it is to get all the little things right, so I really try my best to focus on what I'm doing. I mean, maybe everyone makes a tiny mistake once in a very great while, just being human, right? But I definitely wouldn't call it careless. I care a lot about doing a good job. I would absolutely hate to mess up the line or make things harder for the rest of the team. 

So... no, I don't think I really miss details like that. I really try my best to be thorough and do things right the first time. Is... is it okay that I don't have that problem? I just really want to be a good worker.
Do you often feel like you're driven by a motor, like it's hard to slow yourself down even when you want to?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm like a motor or anything out of control! I just... I have a lot of energy, which I think is a good thing for a production line, right? You want someone who can keep up!

But... sometimes, like if I have to stand perfectly still by my machine for a long time, or if we have to sit through one of those long safety training videos... it does get a little hard. It almost feels like... like there's this pressure building up inside my body? And I just feel like I *have* to move, or pace, or just stretch my legs or go do something right in that exact moment. 

I really try to hold it in, though! I don't want to look like I'm not paying attention or like I'm slacking off. I just... my body just really wants to be doing something productive, I think. Does that make sense? Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?
When someone is talking to you directly, do you often find your mind drifting so that you miss parts of what they said?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really, really hard to listen when people are talking to me! Especially my supervisor or the floor lead, because I want to make sure I know exactly what they need me to do. 

I guess... maybe sometimes if the factory is really loud, or if there's a lot going on around me, I might miss a word or two just because of the noise? But it's not because my mind is drifting! I promise I'm trying my best to pay attention. I always look right at them and nod so they know I'm listening. 

I think I'm a pretty good listener, actually. I really don't want people to think I'm ignoring them, because that would be so rude. It's totally normal to get a little distracted by loud noises though, right? I hope that's an okay answer.

Um... well... I guess maybe they do, sometimes? I really try not to, I promise! I just... I get so excited to be part of the conversation, or I think I know what they're going to say, and it just kind of slips out. 

It happens at work sometimes too, if I'm being completely honest. Like, I'll accidentally jump into my coworkers' conversations, or... or if the lead is explaining something, I might answer before they're even done talking. I don't mean to be rude at all! I just want to show that I understand and that I'm paying attention, you know? 

But... yeah, I think people do get a little irritated with me when I do that. I feel so terrible when I realize I've cut someone off. I'm really trying to work on being a better listener and waiting my turn. I know it's important to let people finish their thoughts. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad person or a terrible friend. I really do mean well. Is... is it normal to struggle with that sometimes?

patient.answer:
Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm like a motor or anything out of control! I just... I have a lot of energy, which I think is a good thing for a production line, right? You want someone who can keep up!

But... sometimes, like if I have to stand perfectly still by my machine for a long time, or if we have to sit through one of those long safety training videos... it does get a little hard. It almost feels like... like there's this pressure building up inside my body? And I just feel like I *have* to move, or pace, or just stretch my legs or go do something right in that exact moment. 

I really try to hold it in, though! I don't want to look like I'm not paying attention or like I'm slacking off. I just... my body just really wants to be doing something productive, I think. Does that make sense? Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?

patient.answer:
Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really, really hard to listen when people are talking to me! Especially my supervisor or the floor lead, because I want to make sure I know exactly what they need me to do. 

I guess... maybe sometimes if the factory is really loud, or if there's a lot going on around me, I might miss a word or two just because of the noise? But it's not because my mind is drifting! I promise I'm trying my best to pay attention. I always look right at them and nod so they know I'm listening. 

I think I'm a pretty good listener, actually. I really don't want people to think I'm ignoring them, because that would be so rude. It's totally normal to get a little distracted by loud noises though, right? I hope that's an okay answer.
